title: Add interactive RAG contract linter & cheat-sheet quickstart
author: Avery Chen
description: Introduce a compact, interactive quickstart that demonstrates using a contract-aware linter for RAG agents and tool-calling contracts. Motivation: teams authoring agents and tool contracts frequently hit silent failures due to mismatched tool signatures, inconsistent structured outputs, and undocumented token expectations. This quickstart provides a runnable dev loop that: 1) validates tool contract JSON schemas against stepwise agent prompts, 2) runs lightweight structured-output fuzz checks, 3) integrates a WASM-based linter shim for fast local iteration, and 4) wires telemetry probes for immediate regression detection. Includes a cheat-sheet for common contract anti-patterns, pre-commit hook example, VSCode snips, and CI job to gate contract regressions. Related: ENG-8421 (contracting diagnostics), PM-124 (docs task). The description includes a short usage flow: git clone && cd quickstarts/rag-contract-linter && yarn && yarn dev to run the live simulator; make lint to run schema checks; yarn smoke to run the synthetic-eval harness. This PR is intended to be self-contained and low-friction for new users while showing recommended patterns for production teams to migrate to Redwood's structured output monitoring. Checklist: - [x] quickstart scaffold and README - [x] linter wasm adapter and small Rust->WASM build artifact (checked-in minimal binary) - [x] CI job and smoke tests - [x] example tool-contracts and agent scenarios - [x] VSCode snippets and pre-commit hook example - [x] telemetry probe presets and sample dashboards (console links in README).
commits: 1) init: add quickstart scaffold and README; 2) feat: wasm linter adapter + binding shim; 3) docs: add cheat-sheet and VSCode snippets; 4) ci: add contract-lint workflow and smoke matrix; 5) fix: adjust schema examples after reviewer feedback; 6) chore: bump dev deps and add test fixtures

ci_checks: contract-lint (matrix: node14,node18) — passed; unit-tests — passed; smoke-eval (small) — passed; build-wasm — passed (CI verifies wasm blob matches source build); docs-lint — passed; a single transient runner failed earlier on node14 then retried and passed; overall CI: pass
release_notes: Adds a new RAG contract-linter quickstart: - runnable dev loop (yarn dev) - wasm-based local linter shim - schema and runtime lint phases - pre-commit hook and VSCode snippets - CI gating workflow and smoke matrix Guidance included in README for migrating to an org-level lint job and enabling telemetry-based regression alerts.
notes_for_maintainers: This quickstart intentionally checks in a very small minimized WASM artifact to reduce friction for first-run users in corporate networks. CI enforces the blob matches source; maintainers may opt to replace the artifact with an upstream submodule. The linter adapter is intentionally non-opinionated about prompting strategy—it emits diagnostics in JSON and provides a suggestion layer for human review. If we want this in the docs landing, add a docs ticket to track integration with 'Playgrounds' index.
example_commands:
git clone <repo> && cd quickstarts/rag-contract-linter && yarn && yarn dev  # runs live simulator
# run lint only
yarn lint:schema
yarn lint:runtime
# run smoke e2e
yarn smoke
local_run_notes: The dev server runs a tiny local HTTP tool-stub and a simulated indexer to exercise tool bindings. Defaults are safe and offline: no cloud keys required. To test streaming and structured-output contract enforcement set ENV DEBUG_RAG_STREAM=1. The README links provide step-by-step screenshots.
audience: engineers and platform teams who maintain agent/tool contract schemas, SDK integrators, and internal DX teams wanting to add contract gating to CI.
testing_and_validation: Added focused smoke scenarios that assert: 1) schema violations produce non-zero exit code; 2) runtime mismatch warnings (non-blocking) when output shape differs; 3) telemetry probes emit expected events (sample fixture). Tests run as part of the contract-lint CI workflow and are lightweight to avoid flakiness.
impact_analysis: Low-risk quickstart; introduces new CI workflow limited to quickstart folder; no infra changes. Telemetry presets are optional and documented. The pre-commit hook is opt-in and added to templates only.
human_readable_summary: Merged an interactive quickstart that helps developers avoid RAG contract regressions by providing a contract linter, example contracts, pre-commit hooks, and CI gates. Designed to be easy to run locally and to scale into org-level CI checks.
privacy_and_compliance: No customer data or keys are stored. The helper indexer uses generated synthetic documents and is offline by default. The wasm artifact is permissively licensed (MIT) and noted in the README.
follow_up_actions: 1) (ENG) consider a separate RFC to standardize contract lint exit codes; 2) (Docs) surface quickstart on the Authoring -> Tooling page; 3) (DX) copy VSCode snippets into the central snippet repo
